Calculadora del código de colores de res: Resistor colour code calculator for 3, 4, 5 and 6 bands: value, tolerance and temperature coefficient, colours of a value with the nearest standard value of the E series, SMD codes, inductors and capacitors, series and parallel combinations, LED resistor and voltage divider, step by step

Resistor colour code calculator: from colours to value with 3, 4, 5 and 6 bands, tolerance and temperature coefficient; from value to colours with the nearest standard value of the E6, E12, E24, E48 and E96 series; 3- and 4-digit SMD codes, with R and EIA-96; inductor colour code and capacitor markings; series and parallel combinations; the best pair of standard values; the resistance for an LED and the voltage divider, step by step.

En serie, R = R₁ + R₂ + …; en paralelo,: In series, R = R₁ + R₂ + …; in parallel, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …. Two 100 Ω resistors in parallel give 50 Ω, and a 330 Ω and a 470 Ω in series give 800 Ω.
Elige los colores de las bandas y obtén: Choose the band colours and get the value, the tolerance and the range in which the real resistance lies. Also the other way round: enter a value and it gives its colours and the nearest standard value. And for SMD resistors, the printed 3- or 4-digit code, with R or EIA-96. Also: inductor colours, the capacitor code, series and parallel combinations, how to obtain a value with two standard ones, the resistance for an LED and a voltage divider.
Son los de la norma IEC 60062. Las cifra: These are from the IEC 60062 standard. The digits run from 0 to 9 in the order black, brown, red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, grey and white: between black and white, the colours of the rainbow.
<b>4 bandas</b> (las más comunes, de car: 4 bands (the most common, carbon, ±5 %): two digits, the multiplier and the tolerance. Yellow, violet, red and gold are 47 × 100 = 4700 Ω = 4.7 kΩ ±5 %.
<b>5 bandas</b> (de película metálica, ±: 5 bands (metal film, ±1 %): three digits, the multiplier and the tolerance.
<b>6 bandas</b>: como las de 5 y una más: 6 bands: like the 5-band ones plus one more for the temperature coefficient.
<b>3 bandas</b>: dos cifras y el multipl: 3 bands: two digits and the multiplier, with no tolerance band, which is then ±20 %.
Se empieza por el extremo contrario a la: You start from the end opposite the tolerance band, which is usually set slightly apart from the others. Gold and silver never come first, and the first band is never black.
Las resistencias no se fabrican de cualq: Resistors are not made in arbitrary values but in those of the E series. The E12 has 12 values per decade, each about $10^{1/12}$ = 1.21 times the previous one, so that the tolerance ranges (±10 %) almost touch. The E24 goes with ±5 %, the E48 with ±2 % and the E96 with ±1 %.
E12: 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, 27, 33, 39, 47,: E12: 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, 27, 33, 39, 47, 56, 68 and 82, multiplied by the appropriate power of 10 (1.2 Ω, 120 Ω, 12 kΩ…).
Las de montaje superficial llevan el val: Surface-mount ones have the value printed on them. With 3 digits (5 %), the first two are the digits and the third the number of zeros: 472 = 47 × 10² = 4.7 kΩ. With 4 digits (1 %) they are three digits and the zeros: 1002 = 10 kΩ. The R acts as the decimal point: 4R7 = 4.7 Ω. In the EIA-96 code, two digits give the position in the E96 series and a letter the multiplier: 01C = 100 × 100 = 10 kΩ.
Las bobinas pequeñas usan los mismos col: Small inductors use the same colours as resistors, with the value in microhenries: brown, black, black and silver are 10 μH ±10 %. Ceramic capacitors have a 3-digit code in picofarads: 104 = 10 × 10<sup>4</sup> pF = 100 nF. A tolerance letter (J ±5 %, K ±10 %, M ±20 %) and a maximum voltage code (1H = 50 V, 2A = 100 V) may follow. The prefix letter is also written in place of the decimal point: 4n7 = 4.7 nF.
Serie, paralelo y valores que no existen: Series, parallel and values that do not exist
En serie las resistencias se suman, $R =: In series resistances add, $R = R_1 + R_2$; in parallel the inverses add, $1/R = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$, which for two is the product over the sum. This is how a value not in the series is obtained: 5 kΩ is not in the E12, but two 10 kΩ in parallel give it exactly.
A un LED le sobra la tensión que no cae: An LED has to lose the voltage that does not drop across it, and the resistor limits it: $R = (V_s − V_{LED})/I$, rounding up to the next standard value so as not to exceed the current. In a divider, $V_{out} = V_{in} R_2/(R_1 + R_2)$; if a load is connected, it sits in parallel with R<sub>2</sub> and the output drops, unless the load is much larger than R<sub>2</sub>.
